newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. jobs data show expansion sustainable - Tyson.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobs data show expansion sustainable - Tyson.

text.p: February's U.S. jobs data suggest the U.S. economy is still expanding and that this expansion is sustainable, former U.S. White House National Economic Advisor Laura Tyson said on Monday.
"It (the jobs data) suggests the continued sustainability of expansion," Tyson told Reuters in an interview.
Tyson, in Singapore to attend a U.S/ASEAN Business Council conference, said that at first glance the jobs data were surprisingly strong.

The data, released on Friday. showed unemployment down to 5.3 percent from from January's 5.4 percent and non-farm payrolls up by 339,000. Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast non-farm payrolls would rise by 230,000.
But Tyson noted there was a downward revision to January's non-farm payrolls -- to 247,000 -- and the mild U.S. winter had led to a big jump in jobs for this time of year in the construction sector.
"An indicator I know the (Federal Reserve) Chairman has been watching of late is the quit rate...which went down," she added.
"Finally the wage increase was obviously one which is totally consistent with productivity growth and no source of inflationary pressure," she said.

She said it was hard to predict what the Federal Reserve would be doing in the near future. "I didn't predict when I was in the government and I'm not going to predict when I'm on the outside," she commented.
